[[Category:Transformer]][[Category:Proper name]]
A Transformer is, at the time of writing(2026-08), the most popular architecture for building [[LLM|Large Language Models]].

== Intuition ==

Rongzhou's ''[[User:Rongzhou/Transformer-Intuition|Transformer is a super-charged next word prediction algorithm]]'' provides a short intuition for Transformers.

<blockquote>
As [[User:Rongzhou/BehindScenes/Transformer-Intuition|the author explains himself]], the story doubles as a live demonstration of Transformers: parts of the story were co-authored by a Transformer model.
</blockquote>

== Mathematical representation ==

A Transformer is a mathematical [[function]] ($f_\theta$) parametrised by [[model parameters]] $\theta$, composed of $N$ independent smaller mathematical functions ('''layers'''):

$$
f_\theta=\varphi^{(N)}\circ\cdots\circ\varphi^{(1)},
$$

=== Layers: $\varphi^{(n)}$ ===

Typically 

$$
1 \text{ Layer}= 2 \text{ Residual connection}
$$ 
(See [[residual connection (Transformer)]])

==== One popular configuration ====

$$
\varphi^{(n)}: X \mapsto X'' \\
\begin{cases}
\mathbf{X}'=\mathbf{X}+\operatorname{Attn}\left(\operatorname{LN}\left(\mathbf{X}\right)\right),\\
\mathbf{X}''=\mathbf{X}'+\operatorname{FFN}\left(\operatorname{LN}\left(\mathbf{X}'\right)\right),
\end{cases}
$$

{| class="wikitable"
|-
| $\operatorname{Attn}$
| '''Attention''', typically [[self-attention]]
|-
| $\operatorname{LN}$
| '''[[Layer-normalisation]]'''
|-
| $\operatorname{FFN}$
| '''[[feed-Forward Network (FFN) Sub-Layer (Transformer)|Feed-Forward Network (FFN)]]'''
|}
